goal.justification: Converted from the tubuild shadow 2026-08-31: the twenty-one written functions are twenty real member functions of dScMgMCarlo_c or of the RTTI-confirmed element class dMgMCarloCardObj_c plus ONE extern "C" definition -- the element destroy stub _ZN18dMgMCarloCardObj_cD1Ev, a hand-written block spelling the ROM's mangled name literally because the header's inline __destroy_arr call passes the destructor as a plain function pointer (the family-ratified destroy-side twin of the factory's ctor stub, the same idiom dScMgCard_c landed as its element stub pair -- and the form the family measured exhaustively there: real member destructors in every spelling fail the byte or the ROM-order gate, the out-of-line form dragging in D0/D2 destructor symbols the cartridge does not carry and the inline form emitting the pair between the scene D1 and scene D0, sliding the scene D0 off ROM address order, notes/minigame-family-decisions.md); free definitions are 0, and the manifest's other two functions are the compiler-emitted destructor pair _ZN13dScMgMCarlo_cD1Ev/D0Ev from the header's inline destructor. All 23 ROM functions match byte-for-byte -- each verified with tools/match.py as it converted, the whole sweep re-verified after the final declaration changes. rawOffsets=0: every raw this+0xoffset chain is now a named header member spelling, and before any raw spelling could be called load-bearing BOTH member forms -- folded and indexed -- were measured; none was needed, every natural member form reproduced the cartridge bytes on the first try, so zero raw spellings are kept (the last three census chains -- the +0x12 lift-table limit and the two +0x18 screen-quotient constants -- are additive constants rather than struct offsets, and decimalized to +18/+24 with the bytes unchanged). externC=1 is the census's only nonzero and is that destroy stub. The renamed functions' ROM symbols were address-only, so their behavioral names are coined from what each function does -- disclosed in the COINED NAMES note below, the per-function banner comments, and symbols/actor_renames.tsv's why column.

2026-08-31 conversion to real members: seventeen of the eighteen tubuild extern "C" free functions became real member functions -- dScMgMCarlo_c's own scene logic (the static board family UpdateBoard/FlipDealtCards/DrawCardValue/BoardReady/BoardBusy/HasRemovablePair/SetupBoard, the member RenderHud, and the adjudicated vtable-slot events OnYoshiTryEat/OnTurnIntoEgg) and the element motion members Render/Update/HitTest/IsPairWith/FlipAway/DealIn/Init over the RTTI-confirmed element class dMgMCarloCardObj_c; the eighteenth, func_ov006_020f7730, is the element destroy stub, renamed to the compiler's own mangling _ZN18dMgMCarloCardObj_cD1Ev and kept as the family-ratified extern "C" spelling because the header's inline __destroy_arr call (in place since the TU's creation, the same recipe as dScMgCard_c/dScMgMCarlo2_c) passes the destructor as a plain function pointer -- the destroy-side twin of the factory's ctor stub in src/func_ov006_020f8ed8.c. Defining the element class and its key function Render in this TU keys the class's _ZTI/_ZTS/_ZTV here as well. Each function was byte-verified with tools/match.py as it converted, and the full 23-function sweep re-verified after the final declaration changes.

COINED NAMES, the one thing not provable: the eighteen renamed functions' ROM symbols were address-only (func_ov006_020f7730..func_ov006_020f8c68), so no recovered spelling exists to confirm or contradict the behavioral names. UpdateBoard, FlipDealtCards, DrawCardValue, BoardReady, BoardBusy, HasRemovablePair, SetupBoard, RenderHud and the element Render/Update/HitTest/IsPairWith/FlipAway/DealIn/Init are coined from what each function does; OnYoshiTryEat/OnTurnIntoEgg are the family's adjudicated legacy recovered names (vtable slots 18/19, notes/minigame-family-decisions.md); the element D1 symbol is the compiler's own mangling of the class this TU's _ZTI/_ZTS proves, and the renamed vtable row is that same class's _ZTV. The coinage is disclosed here, in the per-function banner comments, and in symbols/actor_renames.tsv's why column.

D3 declarations: GXS::LoadOBJPltt, Sound::PlayBank2_2D, ApproachLinear and ApproachLinear2 are declared at their RATIFIED_TRUE_NAMES forms (parameter types read off the mangled names, see the engine-helpers banner in the source); func_ov006_020c0aa8 and func_ov006_020c1804 keep the void* spellings and func_ov006_020c1a88 the char* spelling shared with dScMgBSC_c/dScMgCard_c, because redeclaring a C-linkage symbol with different parameter types is an illegal overloading. Two more C-linkage engine routines split against the siblings and stay split, read off this TU's own ROM call sites: func_ov004_020b66d4 is declared (char*) here because OnYoshiTryEat's ROM site materializes this+0x6000 into r0 -- a dead argument the callee never reads (Card calls the same routine bare) but one the cartridge demonstrably computes, spelled as the member address it is, mArray[76].mTargetY, 0x51a8+0x4c*0x30+0x18=0x6000 -- where dScMgBSC_c/dScMgCard_c spell it (void); and func_ov004_020b56c8 is declared (char*) here because OnTurnIntoEgg's site passes the face-tier table pointer where the siblings spell it (int). Both splits are the family's open question, recorded in notes/minigame-family-decisions.md. The one live local shadow is the Fix12 typedef -- the legacy files' partial Node/Obj shadows are gone with the raw chains they modelled, preserved only in the TUBUILD CONFLICT comments -- and the remaining unk_/pad_ fields (the shared-table reaches unk_4f52/unk_511e, the own-tail board state unk_60a8/unk_60aa/unk_60ae, the base pads pad_4660/pad_4f38) are byte-exact spellings of raw-offset object headers the family has not yet carved; retiring them belongs to a header carve, not this TU.

2026-08-31 verification round, recorded as measured: the conversion-day re-compile under tools/tubuild.py verify re-ran the per-function audit and this block records its round honestly -- functions_matched 22 of 23, relocation_destinations_verified FAIL. The one DIFF row is _ZN18dMgMCarloCardObj_cD1Ev (0x020f7730, the element destroy stub): its bytes matched and its relocation destinations verified, but objisolate.plan() -- the single-function model the verify audit runs per function -- refused the stub's store with 'objisolate: _ZTV18dMgMCarloCardObj_c: unexpected reloc type=2 addend=0'. plan() treats every relocation against a _ZTV defined in the same object as mwcc's own +8 form (the vtable object's offset-to-top/typeinfo preamble) so that its -8 externalisation rewrite applies; addend 0 is refused fail-closed because the single-function model cannot distinguish a hand-written ROM-symbol-convention store from a broken compiler store (objisolate.py:207-212). The production audits for this enrolled consolidated source accept -- and after deadstripping, require -- exactly the stub's form: rombuild.check_object runs derive_deadstrip, whose deadstrip_plan documents both legitimate spellings of a _ZTV store (addend 0 where the source declares the ROM symbol itself, extern int _ZTV18dMgMCarloCardObj_c[] -- symbols.txt's symbol IS the slot array; addend 0 left alone, nonzero addends rebased by 8) and which rebinds _ZTV18dMgMCarloCardObj_c to the ROM address, and then plan_many, which on the now-undefined reference requires addend 0 and refuses nonzero. The linked value is identical either way (both spellings land the vtable address point 0x0213d5ac), which is why the byte comparison, the relocation-destination audit, and the production link all agree while the single-function model alone refuses. dScMgCard_c's committed element stubs (cd398b500) are form-identical -- the same extern int _ZTV...[] declaration plus the (int)_ZTV... store -- and would draw the same per-function refusal; that TU's block records its promotion-era round because its conversion never re-ran the per-function audit. The production authority for this TU is the linkcheck baseline build recorded in the linkcheck block.
